newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends down on poor funds demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends down on poor funds demand.

text.p: Indian call money eased below four percent to end Friday in the 3.75-4.0 percent range on good liquidity and poor demand for funds, dealers said.
They said call money started slightly higher in the 4.0-4.25 percent range but eased as supply was more than adequate to meet the limited demand.
"There is not much demand for funds," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Most banks are either surplus or square."
Dealers said prices of government securities fell in moderate trade on Friday.
"But the rate of fall is less today than in the last couple of days," said a dealer. "The market seems to be bottoming out."
The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock traded on Friday at 102.56 rupees against its last traded price of 102.60 while the 13.50 percent 1998 stock fell to 102.60 from 102.73, dealers said.
Treasury bills maturing in May 1997 were traded at a yield of 8.50 percent while July treasury bills were traded at 9.75 percent.
Dealers said a certificate of deposit maturing on February 7 was traded in the secondary market at a yield of eight percent.
There were no trades in commercial paper, they said.
